newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nintendo revises up 96/97 current profit forecast.
newsitem.headline: Nintendo revises up 96/97 current profit forecast.

text.p: Nintendo Co Ltd said on Wednesday it expected a parent current profit of more than 90 billion yen in the year to March 31, up five billion yen from its previous forecast.
Nintendo will increase shipments of its video game machine Nintendo 64 to one million a month in 1997/98, starting on April 1, from 700,000 units currently, a senior Nintendo executive told Reuters.
Nintendo's forecast revision was based on its assumption that the dollar would stay around 118 yen, he said.
The increase in shipments of the 64-bit game machine for home use was planned to cope with robust demand, especially in the United States, and the launch of the model in Europe in March, he said.
Nintendo is to ask NEC Corp, from which it buys semiconductors, to increase the output of chips for the Nintendo 64, the senior executive said.
Total shipments of Nintendo 64 had reached 3.99 million units by the end of 1996, of which domestic shipments were 1.85 million and shipments to the U.S. market were 2.14 million, he said.
The game machine was launched in Japan in June last year and introduced in the United States in September.
